name: Find a mark that fits more than one explanation

uses.action: Use Kip’s sleeve to put the same chipped pear on clean cloth. A shared mark alone cannot identify a wearer.

name: Follow a mark to the person who put it there

uses.action: Walk the disputed fare to the window. Separate Ise’s guarantor stroke from the copied name of a wearer.

name: Read a tally alongside the action it counted

uses.action: Take one coat across the till twice. The second bit can be refunded while the number of borrowers stays open.

name: Walk two positions with the same object

uses.action: Carry the sleeve along the quick and sheltered routes. Compare their marks with Hesper’s account of carrying for somebody else.
Turn the empty chair sideways and try the inside hook. The same rule looks different to a seated borrower and a standing keeper.

name: Separate a repeatable event from a past event

uses.action: Hold the sponge through Nim’s entrance. Release the drops later. A repeatable backstage shower leaves the first wet coat an open case.

name: Use a record made for a different job

uses.action: Trade the cast sheet for the wardrobe book. Two entries document two different jobs, even though one envelope went to Nim.

name: Protect a person while leaving the claim checkable

uses.action: Cover both names on the refund slip and compare the till against one crossing. The fare can be audited without identifying the borrower.
